Meta.Description: Immutable Source of Truth for Backend API and Database Schema
Meta.Usage: Paste this into the AI Context before generating any API or Data Fetching code.

Protocol.Rule: Single Entry Point (one POST endpoint). RESTful routes (GET /transactions) DO NOT exist.

Authorization: Bearer {JWT}. Each request carries a Supabase session JWT in the Authorization header. The legacy body "key" field is REMOVED. Unauthenticated/invalid-token requests return { status: 'error' }.

family_id is SERVER-DERIVED from the authenticated session and applied server-side. A client-supplied family_id/user_id in the body is ignored/overwritten. Row-Level Security enforces per-family isolation as the backstop.

Row-Level Encryption (v1.14). Sensitive fields ride the per-row `enc` column: an opaque client-encrypted envelope "v1.{b64 iv}.{b64 ciphertext}" (AES-256-GCM, family key, AAD-bound to table:id). The server stores and returns `enc` verbatim, never inspects it, and REJECTS the removed plaintext keys as unknown. Keys never leave family devices; there is no server-side recovery.
Client must use a Request Queue. Network calls are strictly serial.

Strict. Error envelope: { status: 'error', code, message } where `code` is a closed enum - AUTH (401), VALIDATION (400/405, incl. unknown payload keys and malformed bodies), RLS_DENIED (403), CONFLICT (409), INTERNAL (500). Messages are fixed, leak-free texts: VALIDATION carries the authored validation detail; no raw database detail (table, policy, or constraint names) ever reaches the wire.

Action.name: read
Action.Description: Delta Sync. Returns rows modified since timestamp.

Action.name: batchCreate
Action.Description: Bulk Insert. ID is optional (generated by server if missing).

Action.name: batchUpdate
Action.Description: Bulk Edit. Updates ONLY the specific keys provided.

Action.name: batchUpsert
Action.Description: Idempotent Save. Creates if ID missing, Updates if ID exists. Best for Seeding Test Data and sync creates.

Action.name: wipe
Action.Description: Destructive (Test Mode Only). Clears all data in the specified table for the caller's family.

Action.name: version
Action.Description: Lightweight sync probe. Family-scoped; takes no table and no rows. Returns the family high-water mark = max(updated_at) across all tenant tables (or null when the family has no rows), so the client can check on app open whether anything changed since its last sync WITHOUT pulling every collection.

Field.name: enc
Field.description: Opaque encrypted envelope. Plaintext JSON inside (client-only): { line_id: String (groups the instances of one recurring Budget; random, copied on duplication), live: Boolean (this line duplicates into the next period), period_start: String (ISO YYYY-MM-DD), period_end: String (ISO YYYY-MM-DD), target: Number (optional - what the family intends to spend or save this period; absent = the user skipped it, and the card then shows allocated vs actual only), account_ids: String[] (the accounts the Budget aggregates; the first one selected fixed the currency, which is NEVER stored), areas: [{ id: String, name: String, amount: Number, category_ids: String[], icon: String (a lucide icon name; the Area's identity on every card. It is rendered in ONE colour - the Area's HEALTH - so no colour is chosen and none is stored. Optional on the wire and defaulted on read, so a row written without it still opens) }] (the plan; the Area amounts sum to the ALLOCATED total, which is derived and never stored), ignored_category_ids: String[] (optional - categories this Budget DELIBERATELY does not watch. Every category no Area claims is otherwise reported as a planning gap; ignoring one records that the omission was a decision, so it stops being reported. It does NOT stop the money: spend in an ignored category still fails to move the Budget, and the unclaimed-SPEND figure still counts it. Per Budget, never global. Absent = none ignored), adjustments: [{ area_id: String, amount: Number }] (period-local reallocations; they die with their period and are never duplicated forward), note: String (optional) }.

Primary Key. The FIXED literal 'family-settings' - one row per family, so every family writes the same id. The physical primary key is (family_id, id) per migration 0009, which is what stops the second family colliding into an RLS-denied upsert.

The family's display name, and the LIVE one. families.name is the sign-up default and never moves again; this is what a rename writes and what peek_invite reads, falling back to families.name for a family that has not written a settings row yet.
A path to one of the bundled family avatars. Not user imagery: the client's picker is fed a fixed list and there is no upload path, so the value is a choice from a shipped set.

The family's plan. Deliberately PLAINTEXT and deliberately server-readable: it carries the constant 'Alpha Test' today and will carry feature controls and analytics, and a server that cannot read a plan cannot gate a feature on it.

Which way round a date reads for everyone in the family - 'dayFirst' or 'monthFirst'. A value outside that set is refused by the client and resolves to the default. Never reaches an ISO key: interchange stays yyyy-mm-dd.

Primary Key. Random, minted on the creating device. Deliberately NOT derived from the header: a digest of a low-entropy string like 'date' is reversible by wordlist, and deriving it is the one thing that would let the server correlate two families' bank files. Convergence is by client-side dedup on the decrypted header, never by id construction.

Field.name: enc
Field.description: Opaque encrypted envelope. Plaintext JSON inside (client-only): { header: String (the source column header exactly as the file spelled it, kept for display), header_norm: String (the normalised key the memory matches on - lowercased, non-alphanumerics stripped, by the SAME normaliser the suggestion fallback uses, so the two can never disagree about what counts as the same column), verdict: String (either a target field name from the client's closed TARGET_FIELDS set, or the literal 'ignored' - a union, because remembering that a column is deliberately skipped is worth exactly as much as remembering what it maps to) }.

Column.description: Server-managed ISO instant. Also the dedup tiebreaker's first key: the newest row for a given header_norm wins, ties broken by the lexicographically smallest id.
Soft-delete tombstone. A duplicate losing the dedup is tombstoned rather than removed, so every device converges on the same survivor without coordinating.
Standard tenant-table flag; unused by this table today.
